explanation: Spain took the Greater Antilles for gold and tribute, exhausted both, and left islands it barely occupied. The English, French and Dutch founded their seventeenth-century colonies in and around that empty ground. Barbados is the extreme case. The cited account has the Amerindian settlement of the island ending in the early sixteenth century, so the party of 1627 landed on ground with nobody on it. The type is the weak one. Emptiness did not make sugar. It is what sugar was planted in.
